journal.line: I opened Mothwick’s parcel: a lantern with a sleeping baby star inside.
We let Pim sleep. She snored tiny sparks.
I chased off a brute that tried to swallow Pim’s lantern.
We asked the locals the way to the sky.
I bought directions from a snail for 100 coins: left, right, up.
I found stairs behind the cliff. Mothwick pretended he knew.
I beat the Hollow Postmaster’s guard. Mothwick stamped its collar RETURNED.
Pim gave me Starglint: one extra coin on every coin I find, forever.
We ignored the Postmaster’s letter. Mothwick filed it under “Nope”.
I paid the Postmaster’s silly 150-coin fine. Mothwick insisted on a receipt.
I framed the receipt. Then we followed its map anyway.
I fought past the guardians of the cloud stairs.
Pim flew loops around me for a while. I got dizzy.
I gave the Windkeeper one of my Legendary skills. The wind went quiet.
We took the dark corridor. Pim lit the way.
We tried to tiptoe past the Postmaster’s pet. Worms are bad at tiptoeing.
The Postmaster’s pet and its friends lost. Mothwick gave it a biscuit anyway.
I lent Pim most of my warmth to mend Mothwick’s wing.
Pim made my Starglint brighter: two extra coins on every coin I find.
We wondered whether the Hollow Postmaster was really a villain.
Mothwick told me the Postmaster’s story. Pim still comes first.
I gave a Mythic skill to open the Star Gate.
I beat the Postmaster’s last guard behind the Star Gate.
We met the Hollow Postmaster. He had dropped Pim long ago.
I hugged the Hollow Postmaster. It was like hugging a draught.
Pim told us I fell from the sky too, long ago. That explains a lot.
We beat the Light-Eater at the Top of the Sky.
Mothwick and I decided to light Pim’s way together.
Mothwick gave his letters and I gave every skill I had. It was very bright.
Pim kissed my nose and went home. Three extra coins on every coin I find, for ever.
